formulations.text: A measurable space is a pair (X,Σ), where X is a set and Σ is a σ-algebra of subsets of X.

context: Normalized measure space with total mass one
editorial_screening_reason: ProofWiki defines a probability space as a measure space with total measure one. Probability measure countable additivity and nonnegativity are part of the measure definition; normalized total mass is a distinctive condition. This can be a target for stochastic-process and conditional-expectation meanings after independently screening the measurable-space and measure prerequisites. The empty space admits no probability measure with P(Ω)=1, so it is excluded by the axioms, not by an arbitrary extra clause.

formulations.text: A probability space is a triple (Ω,Σ,P) where (Ω,Σ) is a measurable space and P is a countably additive measure on Σ satisfying P(Ω)=1.

context: Random variable with values in an arbitrary measurable space
editorial_screening_reason: The direct ProofWiki random-variable page separates the general measurable-space-valued and real-valued formulations. Real-valued measurability has an equivalent half-infinite-interval inverse-image criterion. These two variants have different codomain scopes; do not merge their object contexts silently or confuse a 'continuous random variable' with a continuous sample path. General random variable and real-valued random variable can be displayed in appropriate educational ordering and linked to probability/measurable spaces when independently screened. A random variable with general measurable target and a real-valued random variable have genuinely different codomain constraints; record as distinct contextual meanings in one displayed term group.

formulations.text: A real-valued random variable on (Ω,F,P) is an F/B(R)-measurable map X:Ω→R, where B(R) is the Borel σ-algebra; equivalently the preimage of every interval (−∞,a] belongs to F.
